good_heights.top_why: every sub-segment of the top leg has Re(zeta conj c) > 0 for its axis direction c, so zeta has no zero on [1/2, 2] x {50}; Re s >= 1 is zero-free (Mathlib) and the zeros are symmetric under s -> 1 - conj s, so no nontrivial zero has ordinate T
good_heights.bottom_why: the same, on the bottom leg; and zeta has no zero with 0 < Im s <= T1 (low_height below)

skeleton.why: the same half-plane argument, on the skeleton contour's legs, every sub-segment in Re zeta > 0

plan_of_record: skeleton_contour: the heights the skeleton states (lean/RHHeight/Skeleton.lean and PLAN.md); lean_contour at T1 = 10 is an independent route and the fallback

skeleton_contour.source: hunts/rh_height_lean/PLAN.md, sections 4, 5 and 7 (2026-10-21), and lean/RHHeight/Skeleton.lean, whose count_eq_ten_of concludes Ncount 3 52 = 10

contour.formula: Ncount T1 T2 = (theta(T2) - theta(T1))/pi + Q/2 + (A2 - A1)/pi

gamma_side.identity: gamma_side (vendored): (1/pi) Im halfContour (logDeriv Gammaℝ) T1 T2 = int_{T1}^{T2} mu, and int mu = (theta(T2) - theta(T1))/pi
gamma_side.stirling_main_formula: G(T2) - G(T1), G(t) = (t log(t/(2 pi)) - t)/(2 pi)

sensitivity.note: an error e in a Lean bound for log(2 pi) moves the Stirling main term by about (T2 - T1) e/(2 pi); the margin above tolerates it while that stays well below the margin

contour.projection_basis: prime exp towers times hunt #133's measured 52 s per 17 towers; for Taylor orders above 1 the derivative boxes add products this does not count

low_height.note: the zero-count routine's contour runs along the real axis, so N(T1) = 0 there is an enclosure-carrying statement that no zero has 0 < Im s < T1; the Lean proof still needs its own low-height exclusion

routine.role: zero count N(T) by the argument principle, Riemann-von Mangoldt form N(T) = 1 + theta(T)/pi + S(T)

rigor_template.bottom: none: the routine's contour starts at s = 2 on the real axis, and the 1 in N(T) = 1 + theta(T)/pi + S(T) carries the real-axis part
rigor_template.top_height_why: condition 1 holds on every sub-segment (the Arb box of zeta over the whole sub-segment misses 0, box_abs_lower > 0), so zeta has no zero on [1/2, 2] x {T}; with Re s >= 1 zero-free and the zeros symmetric under s -> 1 - conj s, T is not the ordinate of any nontrivial zero

routine.role: RH to height T: proven sign changes of Hardy's Z on (0, T) against the zero count
